master_sections.heading: STRATEGIC DECISION
master_sections.original_text:
STOP patch-by-patch treatment of individual Anthropic-compatible stream edge cases.

The recent failures all belong to the SAME shared protocol state-machine domain:

- cumulative usage updates;
- message_stop terminal semantics;
- post-terminal ping;
- Provider error precedence;
- non-object error payloads;
- post-terminal timeout;
- post-terminal cancellation;
- capture completeness;
- precise failure-cause preservation.

Therefore this task MUST close the shared Anthropic-compatible streaming state machine as a bounded,
explicit, mechanically testable CLOSED-WORLD protocol boundary.

The goal is NOT to enumerate every possible Python exception.

The goal IS:

For every protocol state and every supported/known event class that can cross this shared production
stream boundary, the runtime has exactly one explicit source-grounded behavior:

- ACCEPT / ADVANCE
- IGNORE_TRANSPORT_KEEPALIVE
- TERMINAL_SUCCESS
- TERMINAL_PROVIDER_ERROR
- TERMINAL_TRANSPORT_FAILURE
- FAIL_CLOSED_PROTOCOL_INVALID
- VERSIONED_UNKNOWN_EVENT_POLICY

No implicit fallthrough.
No generic "anything after terminal is invalid" shortcut.
No generic "unknown child => transport."
No AttributeError from payload shape assumptions.
No post-terminal timeout/cancel downgrading an already complete result.
No later transport tail replacing an already observed Provider error.

If this closed-world proof fails, STOP.
Do NOT return to another narrow patch task.

master_sections.heading: THREE SEPARATE COMPLETENESS CONCEPTS
master_sections.original_text:
Mechanically separate:

1. SEMANTIC_TERMINAL_COMPLETE
   The semantic Provider response has reached a valid terminal state.

2. TERMINAL_CAPTURE_COMPLETE
   All bytes/events required to prove the terminal semantic result were durably captured.

3. TRANSPORT_TAIL_CLOSED_CLEANLY
   The underlying transport closed cleanly after terminal.

If current schema can represent these with existing fields, reuse it.
Do not invent parallel state unnecessarily.

Required invariants:

- post-terminal timeout/cancel must not downgrade an already complete semantic result/capture;
- pre-terminal timeout/cancel remains failure;
- Provider error already observed remains primary even if tail timeout occurs;
- ping after terminal may be diagnostic/ignored only if source-grounded.

Create:
shared-completeness-contract-v1.json

master_sections.heading: CAUSAL PRECEDENCE CONTRACT
master_sections.original_text:
Define explicit narrow precedence.

Examples:

A. Provider error -> ping -> timeout
PRIMARY = Provider error
TAIL = ping + timeout diagnostics

B. message_stop complete -> ping -> timeout
PRIMARY = successful semantic terminal
TAIL = ping + timeout diagnostics

C. message_stop complete -> cancellation
PRIMARY = successful semantic terminal
TAIL = cancellation diagnostic

D. timeout before terminal
PRIMARY = timeout/transport failure

E. cancellation before terminal
PRIMARY = cancellation/transport failure

F. message_stop -> Provider error
Must follow source-grounded policy and must NOT silently ignore the Provider error.

Do not generalize "first exception always wins" outside this stream boundary.

Produce:
shared-stream-causal-precedence-contract-v1.json
